summary.text: Jim McDermott is the Libertarian nominee for Alaska's at-large U.S. House seat. A 22-year U.S. Air Force veteran and business instructor at the University of Alaska, he ran for the seat as a Libertarian in 2012, 2014 and 2016. He finished eighth in the August 2026 primary and joined the general-election ballot after a higher-finishing candidate withdrew.

paragraphs.text: McDermott holds a B.S. in occupational education from Wayland Baptist University and an M.S. in business organizational management from the University of La Verne. He served 22 years in the U.S. Air Force and works as a business instructor for the University of Alaska.

McDermott first ran as the Libertarian candidate for Alaska's at-large U.S. House seat in 2012, losing to Rep. Don Young. In 2014 he won the Libertarian nomination unopposed and received 7.6% of the vote (21,290 votes) in the general election, finishing third behind Young and Forrest Dunbar. He ran again in 2016 and again lost to Young.
In 2026 he took 1.2% of the vote in the August primary and replaced Democrat John Brendan Williams on the general-election ballot after Williams withdrew.
